Is it just the exhaust pipe, or does that also include a catalytic converter? Sometimes these are also one whole piece, especially if they're connected to the exhaust manifold of the vehicle.  If you live in a state where they put salt on the roads, then a rusty exhaust system can happen around the decade mark. Ask a few more questions about what is actually being replaced and if they are aftermarket parts, or original manufacturer parts. That too can make a big difference.

On a lot of front wheel drive vehicles, the exhaust manifold will have a catalytic converter built right onto it, mostly due to packaging reasons, but also for emissions as the catalytic converter heats up faster when it's closer to the engine. These kinds of systems usually meet at a collector, then a single exhaust goes out to the back of the vehicle.  The OP wasn't specific enough about what part of his exhaust system was bad, so it's kind of difficult to gauge if that's too expensive or not. If it's just a muffler from the collector back, that should be a few hundred bucks tops to repair or replace. Catalytic converters can be extremely expensive as they contain rare earth metals.

As a resident of my country, I use both measurement systems for every day life and I'm fine with using both. The only thing I don't like about the other system is speed and distance. It's not that there's anything wrong with it, but it just isn't as intuitive to me to figure out how long it will take me to get to a destination 560 units away, travelling at 80 units per hour. It's like I have these predetermined segments built in my head to tell me how long that kind of trip would take in the other units.

When I was driving through another country a few years ago, I'd simply convert everything to my local system by looking down at my dash, as cars in my region have both units on the gauge cluster. It was somehow easier for me to convert everything to my local units from the other units, then I could figure out how long it would take me to get to my destination. I realize this is wholly impractical, and rather counterintuitive, but it somehow works in my brain. Also, that other country is just as weird as the UK when it comes to their measuring systems. Much of the time things were metric, but there were other times were it was both. "Yeah, so go down that highway for a few clicks, then you'll see this barn, so turn there and go down that road a few miles, where you'll see a lake a few miles off to your left, drive another few k, then you'll see the airport hanger on your right."
